summary: Implemented in #710 (60633eff3). The server writes http-bound, http-serving, startup-ready, startup-phase and fatal frames on fd 4. Desktop parses them with the shared parser and feeds them into BackendReadinessTracker. The stdout 'Listening on' match stays as a fallback, the HTTP probe only starts after 3 s, and fatal frames or exit code 78 halt the crash loop. The httpStartupGate removes the dead-window hang that made probes cost 1 s. The user's real desktop log confirms that normal boots now fire no HTTP probes. Nuance: in practice the stdout line still wins the race by 0-3 ms on all 16 post-#710 launches (source=listening every time), so the frame works as an always-present backstop rather than as the signal actually used. The robustness goal still holds: if the log line goes away, readiness falls through to the frame about 1 ms later instead of to the HTTP poll. The edge-path issues left are minor.
correction: The auditor says desktop 'resolves readiness from http-serving'. That is true of the design, but the logs show otherwise in practice. HttpRouter.serve wraps the serve layer in HttpServer.withLogAddress, so 'Listening on' is logged before httpServingLayer (server.ts:715-724) writes the http-serving frame. Of the 16 launches in ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/desktop-main.log that carry http-serving frames, all record 'bootstrap backend ready source=listening'; the frame lands 0-3 ms after the stdout line. The auditor also missed that the no-tracker path still starts the 100 ms HTTP poll immediately (see fixDefects). Neither point changes the DONE classification.

evidence.note: DesktopBackendLifecycleFrame union (http-bound, http-serving, startup-ready, startup-phase, fatal) and parseDesktopBackendLifecycleFrame; DESKTOP_BACKEND_FATAL_EXIT_CODE=78.
fd 4 Socket created and attachDesktopLifecycleChannel called; invoked from cli.ts:510-512 once the bootstrap envelope says desktop mode.
http-bound written after bind; the startup gate is installed before listen (server.ts:258) and the early static handler serves the shell.
http-serving written by httpServingLayer, which is provided by HttpRouter.serve, so it only runs after the handlers are attached (and after Effect's withLogAddress has logged 'Listening on').
Requests and upgrades that arrive before the handlers exist are held and replayed (503 after 10 s or overflow), so a probe no longer hangs in the dead window.
startup-ready is written when the command gate opens.
Deterministic failures write a fatal frame and exit 78.
The fd-4 reader passes non-sample frames through the shared parser to onFrame.
handleBackendFrame records phase marks, sends http-serving and fatal to readiness.handleFrame, and loads the window on http-bound.
BackendReadinessTracker: settles on http-serving (with a port check), keeps ServerListeningDetector as the fallback, rejects on fatal.
The HTTP probe is deferred by the delay and cancelled when the tracker settles.
Residual: with no readiness tracker (readyPromise null), the 100 ms / 1 s HTTP poll still starts at once, as it did before.

Residual path: if the adopted early child is already gone, startBackend returns without a wait, and bootstrap's ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen (and app 'activate' during a restart backoff) then waits with backendReadiness=null. That is an HTTP-only wait, and backendReadyChild ends up null.

16 post-#710 launches have desktop.backend.http-serving 0-3 ms after desktop.backend.listening; all 445 recorded launches report source=listening and none report source=http. Boots take 246-956 ms, so the 3 s HTTP fallback never started.
Unit tests cover frame-driven readiness, the fatal and port-mismatch paths, and the delayed HTTP fallback. No server-side test asserts frame order (http-serving only after the handlers attach).

fixDefects:
Minor, edge paths only:
(1) The no-tracker path still polls HTTP from t=0. waitForBackendStartupReady (apps/desktop/src/backendStartupReadiness.ts:20-23) runs waitForHttpReady at once when readyPromise is null. This happens when ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen runs while no child is tracked: bootstrap's call at main.ts:4872 after the adopted early child has already died (startBackend bails at main.ts:3360-3364), or app 'activate' (main.ts:4931) during a restart backoff. That boot then uses 100 ms / 1 s probes, and the restarted child's frames never settle the in-flight wait, because startBackend's own ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen returns early while that wait is in flight. waitForBackendWindowReady also captures `backendProcess` (null) at call time (main.ts:1600, 1613), so backendReadyChild is null and a later post-ready crash of the replacement counts once as a pre-ready failure.
(2) Attribution only: stdout 'Listening on' is logged before the http-serving frame is written, so readiness source=listening on every real boot. The frame is a backstop rather than the primary signal, and the stdout scan still runs on every boot.
(3) Fatal frames for failures before fd 4 is attached (bootstrap-envelope-missing, env ConfigError before cli.ts:511) are no-ops. Exit code 78 still halts restarts and the stderr tail carries the reason.
implementationSketch:
Optional cleanup, Effort S:
(a) In apps/desktop/src/main.ts ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen: if backendReadiness === null (no live child), only call ensurePackagedBootstrapWindowOpen and return. startBackend already calls ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen (main.ts:3367) once a child and tracker exist. Alternatively, remove the immediate-HTTP branch in waitForBackendStartupReady for the packaged path.
(b) Store the child on the tracker, or capture it at startBackend, and set backendReadyChild from the child whose tracker settled instead of from `backendProcess` at call time.
(c) To make the frame primary: in apps/server/src/server.ts call HttpRouter.serve(..., { disableListenLog: true }) and log `Listening on http://host:port` from httpServingLayer right after writeDesktopLifecycleFrame. Older desktops keep the log line; new desktops see the frame first.
Tests: add a backendStartupReadiness test for 'no tracker means no immediate poll', or a main-level unit for the guard; add a server test that the http-serving frame is written after the request/upgrade listeners are attached and before the 'Listening on' log.
decisionReason: Desktop-local readiness plumbing and server log ordering only; no auth/E2EE, hosted lifecycle, or Hub protocol impact.
